searchText: <@!363800010518822915> <@!203220829473996800>; how's - 15/1 -- midday PST - 16/1 -- 7am Sydney - 15/1 -- 9pm Amsterdam works for me Works for me, but no problem to move to 10 or 11pm if 7 is too early for you Is array based stateful dag the one everyone's keen on? I'll spend some time review the code today https://github.com/protolambda/lmd-ghost#array-based-stateful-dag-proto_array <@!363800010518822915> I recommend the Rust code from Paul (see open PR in their client repo), that Go code of mine was the original take, and it works, but it's less readable, and not adapted to the new forkchoice features. Tree filter, bounce protection, and justified-state based balance updates. Paul has done a great job updating it. Although there still is a bug in the block-tree-filter usage that is being looked into. Np. I'll read both implementations. I'm a rust noob so Go may still be better for me 😂 Main difference is that the rust packs the different arrays into a single array of structs. I was just messing with minimalism at the time of design (a working dag as just an array...) and split it in different arrays. Aside from localizing reads/writes, there's little benefit, and the Rust is more readable and has nice safety checks and errors. Edit: localizing reads/writes is also interesting, the struct may actually work better for the single-loop mixed usage the algorithm is. But not micro-benching it. Just go with readability 👍 What's the difference between best child versus best target/descendant? best target is poor naming, it's more like "best head"; skipping right to the end of the tree I wasn't concerned as much with ffg as just pure ghost and the dag structure when naming the variables in go code Wouldn't they be the same? I guess I'm not understanding why there needs to be two ways to express "best child/descendent/head" best child is the direct node under a parent, used in some checks (this is GhoST, with GST for greedy subtree, thus immediate child weight counts, not the eventual head) and then the other is to just have that nice O(1) head lookup, to not walk best-childs (although cost wouldn't be high) Got it. Thanks
